extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners applying recurrence plots (RPs), cross-recurrence plots (CRPs) and recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) to time series in neuroscience, geophysics, engineering, economics, astrophysics and related fields
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for applying recurrence plots, cross-recurrence plots and RQA to real-world time series (choice of embedding, thresholds, measures, surrogate testing, sliding-windows, LOS extraction and interpretation) across multiple application domains (EEG/ERP, finance, geophysics, engineering, astrophysics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of vertical-structure-based RQA measures to detect transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures based on vertical RP structures uncover transitions which are not found by RQA measures based only on the diagonal RP lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, LAM and T T (vertical-structure measures) can reveal transitions into and out of laminar states (e.g. after surprising stimuli in ERP data), while diagonal-structure measures such as DET and L may be less apparent. Report spatial/temporal differences in where and when vertical measures indicate transitions; compare diagonal- and vertical-based measures to ensure transitions are not missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply RQA to single-trial ERP data instead of relying solely on ensemble averaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensemble averaging filters out high-frequency structures and requires many trials, which is problematic in clinical or child studies or when repeating affects performance; RQA concepts can analyse event-related activity on a single-trial basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single-trial RPs and compute measures (DET, L, LAM, TT) per trial to detect transient structures (e.g. N100, P300). Example: 25-electrode ERP with 4 ms sampling; observe clustered recurrence points around ERP components. Emphasise that non-stationarity around ERP components may show as white bands in RPs; vertical measures (LAM, TT) can detect P300 in single trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select RQA measures and embedding for nonlinearity testing of exchange rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute RR, DET, ENT and Lmax (RQA measures) for each exchange-rate series using embedding parameters (example: m = 20, τ = 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine recurrence threshold ε as the smallest value at which all RQA parameters are non-zero. Produce a large number of surrogate series (example: 500) by shuffling the time series (preserves distribution, destroys temporal dependencies) and compute RQA measures on surrogates to form empirical distributions. If all original RQA measures exceed the 95th percentile of the surrogate distributions, reject the assumption of a linear stochastic process driving the series. Report RR and DET as percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surrogate testing procedure for significance assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use surrogates to create empirical null distributions for RQA measures under specific null hypotheses (e.g. independence in time but same distribution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example procedure: create 500 surrogate series by shuffling the original data (preserves marginal distribution but removes temporal dependence), compute the same RQA measures using identical embedding and RP parameters, and compare original measures to the surrogate empirical distribution (e.g. 95th percentile). Use the joint exceedance of several RQA measures (e.g. RR, DET, ENT, Lmax) as a stricter criterion for rejecting a null hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct phase-space vectors from multichannel sensor data for damage detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Form the phase-space vector by using all sensor measurements as components (multi-dimensional phase-space) when sensors monitor the same system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: nine sensors → 9-dimensional phase space. Compute cross-recurrence plots (CRPs) between each damage stage and the undamaged case; quantify using RQA measures (RR, DET, ENT_R) in sliding windows to identify deviations as damage increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sliding-window RQA to obtain time-resolved detection of changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute RQA measures within sliding windows to assess evolving changes and detect onset of damage or transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example parameters: window length 10,000 with shift of 1,400 points. Report how measures (RR, DET, ENT_R) change with damage magnitude; sliding-window choice affects temporal resolution and sensitivity—report and justify choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: RR and DET are sensitive indicators for early damage detection (compare to benchmark measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: RR and DET can clearly identify and quantify damage scenarios (example: damages larger than 10% in a simulated plate) and often show larger relative changes than standard modal frequencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare percent changes of RR and DET with changes in modal frequencies f1,f2,f3 as benchmarks. Note ENT_R may be less sensitive (detectable clearly only at large damage levels). Present percent changes to quantify sensitivity (example: RR up to 33%, DET up to 22%, modal freq changes <10%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CRPs to align time scales of geophysical profiles via LOS extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross recurrence plots contain information about the time transformation needed to align the time scales of two data series, revealed by a distorted main diagonal (line of synchronization, LOS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolate and track the LOS (e.g. with an LOS-tracking algorithm) to obtain a nonparametric rescaling function for re-alignment. Example embedding for rock-magnetic data: m = 3, τ = 5, resulting in final reconstructed dimension 6. Prefer CRP-based automatic alignment over subjective 'wiggle matching'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate LOS quality when using CRP for dating or time-alignment (Q factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess potential LOS candidates by a quality factor Q = N• / (N• + N◦) × 100%, where N• is the number of black dots on the line and N◦ the number of gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger Q indicates a better LOS (Q = 100% means a continuous line). Also evaluate smoothness: use average second derivative of the time-transfer function as a criterion (abrupt changes in slope are undesirable for sedimentation rates). Use both Q and smoothness to select the most plausible LOS among candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neighbourhood criterion and choice of recurrence rate (RR) in CRP/RP construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The neighbourhood criterion (e.g. FAN) and chosen recurrence rate (e.g. 30%, 40%) determine the binary recurrence structure used for LOS finding and other analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: use FAN with 30% RR (grey RP) and 40% RR (bright grey RP) for magneto-stratigraphy matching. Report the criterion and target RR used and, if relevant, show results for differing RR to assess robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of embedding parameters (dimension m and delay τ) matters and should be reported/empirically chosen
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose embedding dimension m and delay τ appropriate to the data; embedding choice affects the amount and type of line structures in RPs/CRPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically select parameters (examples in text: m = 3, τ = 5 for geological profiles; m = 4, τ = 6 for magneto-stratigraphy; m = 20, τ = 1 for exchange rates). Note: a rather small embedding decreases the amount of line structures representing negative-time progress. Always state chosen m and τ and justify empirically or via standard methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine recurrence threshold ε using a rule ensuring nontrivial RQA measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Set ε (recurrence threshold) such that RQA parameters are meaningful (example rule: ε is the smallest value at which all RQA parameters are non-zero).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the rule used to pick ε and the resulting recurrence rate. Consider sensitivity analyses across ε values and document how choices affect measures and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation and reporting of RQA measures and units
rubrics_metrics.description: Different RQA measures capture different dynamical properties: RR (recurrence rate), DET (determinism), ENT (entropy), Lmax (longest diagonal), LAM (laminarity), TT (trapping time) etc.; RR and DET are often reported in percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which measures were used and why (e.g. vertical measures for laminar transitions, diagonal for predictability). Compare and contrast measures where appropriate (e.g. vertical vs diagonal measures) and report units/normalisations (e.g. RR and DET in %).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CRP-based similarity measures (e.g. RRc_τ and Lc_τ) to detect lagged similarity between paleodata and modern proxies
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute cross-recurrence-based similarity measures across lags; extreme values at specific lags indicate significant similarity and potential coupling (e.g. ENSO influence on palaeo-precipitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot similarity measures as a function of lag and identify maxima/minima corresponding to typical delays (example: peaks at lag ≈ 0 and minima around 8–12 months). Use comparison with modern instrumental records to support palaeo-inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate correlation entropy K2 from RPs for predictability/stability analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use automated K2-estimation algorithms on recurrence plots to estimate correlation entropy as a measure of predictability; K2 can sensitively indicate resonances and chaotic behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example application: stability of extra-solar planetary orbits—K2 is more sensitive than maximum eccentricity in diagnosing high-order resonances and un/stability regions. Use automated algorithms (reference to Appendix B.4) and complement K2 with other stability indicators (e.g. maximum eccentricity) to form robust conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect synchronization transitions with recurrence-based indices (CPR, JPR) and validate against other methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute indices such as CPR (for phase synchronization) and JPR (for generalized synchronization) across varying coupling strengths to detect transitions to PS and GS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: in electrochemical oscillators varying coupling µ revealed transitions near µ = 0.6 for both PS and GS. Compare recurrence-based findings with alternative methods (e.g. mutual false nearest neighbors) and report agreements or discrepancies.
